subject: Latency & throughput alignment for Dedicated pilot — Novasys
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@novasys.ai>, Ops Team <ops@novasys.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & three concrete perf questions

Thanks again for the demo today — we appreciated the clarity on your 99th/95th latency targets and the mixed workload profile. Quick recap plus the three items we need to lock down before the pilot: 

1) Latency SLO target: you mentioned p95 ~200ms for single-stream chat calls (token-by-token streaming). Can you confirm whether the 200ms is server-side time only or includes network/transit we should budget for?

2) Throughput & concurrency: your throughput target looks like ~120 QPS sustained with occasional spikes to 350 QPS for 90s windows. Is the critical constraint concurrent active streams (long lived) or total token/sec?

3) Streaming behavior: are you doing server-driven token streaming with client-side aggregation? We need to know whether small-batch token latency (first-token) or steady-state token throughput matters more.

Attached: I exported the metrics you shared (novasys-metrics-export.csv) and a short GPU comparison I ran against a similar workload (gpu-bench-compare.pdf). Proposed next steps below.

Immediate asks (can you reply inline):
- Confirm whether the p95 target is server-only or E2E.
- Confirm expected mean tokens per request (approx).
- Pick a pilot GPU preference (if any) — otherwise we'll propose H100 x2 baseline + A100 x2 as fallbacks.

Next actions from Redwood: we will scope a dedicated pilot (reserved pool) and propose a minimal configuration that hits your p95 under sustained 120 QPS and the spike profile. Ben and Karthik will own the sizing bench and pilot plan.

Thanks,
— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Kim <sarah@novasys.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-30T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & three concrete perf questions

On Thu, Nov 30, 2028 at 09:12 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo today — we appreciated the clarity on your 99th/95th latency targets...

Thanks Soojin — great summary. Answers inline below:

1) The 200ms p95 is intended as E2E (server + minimal network). Our clients are all US-west; add ~30ms for client-side network on average. Server-side SLA we hope to see ~160ms p95.

2) Concurrency: our usage is dominated by concurrent long-lived chat sessions (users keep open connections). Typical active concurrent sessions are 220, with bursts to 700 for event-driven pushes. Token-per-request average is 120 tokens (incl. system + user + expected generation).

3) Streaming: yes, token streaming (server push) is the delivery mode. First-token latency is important for perceived responsiveness, steady-state tokens/sec matters for cost.

We don't have a hard GPU preference; cost matters but hitting p95 E2E is the priority. We can start with H100 if you believe it materially reduces p95 for streaming workloads.

Attached: I included export from our ops team (same CSV). We'll schedule a short sync next week.

— Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Product, Novasys AI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: sizing hypothesis for Novasys pilot (draft)

Soojin / Karthik — based on Sarah's clarifications: 220 sustained concurrent streams, bursts to 700, avg 120 tokens per request, E2E p95 target 200ms (server-side target ~160ms). My back-of-envelope: 

- Pilot baseline: H100 x2 (reserved pool) to focus on first-token latency for streaming + larger KV cache headroom. Configure smaller batch windows (10–20ms) to prioritize first-token.
- Cost-optimized variant: A100 x4 with aggressive batching and 16-bit quantization for lower spend; may hit steady-state throughput but risk first-token p95.
- Hypothesis: H100 baseline should meet server-side p95 ~150–160ms at 120 QPS sustained, but we need to validate spikes to 700 conc. We'll propose a small stress bench: 1) sustained 120 QPS for 1h, 2) spike profile 350 QPS for 90s x3, 3) concurrency ramp to 700 for 2m.

Action items for pilot doc:
- Karthik: produce bench script that reproduces token streaming pattern + KV cache warmup.
- Me: produce cost comparison (H100 vs A100) and short runbook for fallbacks (auto-shift to quantized model if over threshold).
- Soojin: confirm network budget assumptions and collect any synthetic prompt sets.

I attached a quick GPU comparison I ran earlier (gpu-bench-compare.pdf) — it's rough but shows H100 advantage on first-token time for our streaming harness.

Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah@novasys.ai>
Date: 2028-11-30T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & three concrete perf questions

Thanks, all — quick technical clarifications and a proposed bench plan below.

Bench objectives (what we'll measure):
- First-token latency (cold vs warmed KV cache) p50/p95/p99 server-side.
- Steady-state token throughput (tokens/sec) and cost per 1M tokens for each GPU profile.
- Concurrency ceiling (how many simultaneous streams before p95 breaches 160ms).

Bench plan (deliverable in 7 business days):
1) Micro-bench: single-rep bench on H100 x2 and A100 x4 with realistic prompt distribution (I need the sample prompt set).
2) Sustained 1h profile at 120 QPS.
3) Spike test: 350 QPS for 90s x3 and concurrency ramp to 700 for 2 minutes.

Config notes:
- We'll test with prefix/KV cache enabled and disabled to show delta.
- Batching window defaults: 15ms (low-latency) and 50ms (throughput-optimized) — will test both.

Sarah — can you drop a small representative prompt set (5–10 prompts) and confirm if your payloads include heavy function/tool calls (no for now?)

I'll include the bench artifacts as CSV and short PDF. Also adding the proposed pilot schedule (MAP-pilot-schedule.xlsx) to attachments.

— Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Kim <sarah@novasys.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & three concrete perf questions

Karthik — thanks. Attached the prompt set and a quick note on function calls (none in the pilot). We're good with the bench plan and H100 baseline.

On Thu, Nov 30, 2028 at 14:22 Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Bench objectives (what we'll measure):
> - First-token latency (cold vs warmed KV cache) p50/p95/p99 server-side...

I also confirm network budget: please assume 30ms median client network. Looking forward to the artifacts.

— Sarah
Head of Product, Novasys AI
